```{r echo = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

# Load data
sal <- read_csv(paste0(
  "https://stat.cmu.edu/~sgallagh/courses/mads-fall-2026/",
  "datavis-36613/data/salaries.csv.gz"
))
```

```{r echo = FALSE}
sal <- sal |>
  mutate(
    experience_level = factor(
      experience_level,
      levels = c("EX", "SE", "MI", "EN"),
      labels = c("Executive", "Senior", "Mid", "Entry")
    ),
    
    remote = case_when(
      remote_ratio == 0 ~ "On-Site",
      remote_ratio == 50 ~ "Hybrid",
      remote_ratio == 100 ~ "Fully remote"
    ),
    
    remote = factor(
      remote,
      levels = c("On-Site", "Hybrid", "Fully remote")
    ),
    
    log_salary = log(salary_in_usd)
  ) |>
  filter(employment_type == "FT")
```

```{r echo = FALSE}
sal <- sal |>
  mutate(
    role_group = case_when(

      # Data Science
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(job_title),
        "data scientist|decision scientist|applied scientist"
      ) ~ "Data Science",

      # AI / Machine Learning
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(job_title),
        "machine learning|\\bml\\b|artificial intelligence|\\bai\\b|nlp|computer vision|deep learning|llm|prompt"
      ) ~ "AI / Machine Learning",

      # Data Engineering / Infrastructure
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(job_title),
        "data engineer|data architect|dataops|data infrastructure|data platform|data integration|etl|data pipeline|data developer"
      ) ~ "Data Engineering / Infrastructure",

      # Analytics / BI
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(job_title),
        "analyst|analytics|business intelligence|\\bbi\\b|power bi|data analysis|reporting|data visualization"
      ) ~ "Analytics / BI",

      # Research / Quantitative
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(job_title),
        "research|quantitative|statistician|statistical|computational scientist|economist|actuar|postdoctoral"
      ) ~ "Research / Quantitative",

      # Management / Product
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(job_title),
        "manager|director|head of|product manager|product owner|data lead|analytics lead"
      ) ~ "Management / Product",

      # Software / Systems Engineering
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(job_title),
        "software|developer|engineer|devops|platform|site reliability|systems|system engineer|architect|technical lead|tech lead"
      ) ~ "Software / Systems Engineering",

      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )
```







```{r fig-career-dashboard}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 10
#| out-width: 100%

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(scales)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare data
# --------------------------------------------------

levels <- c("Entry", "Mid", "Senior", "Executive")
sizes <- c("All Companies", "Small", "Medium", "Large")

salary_data <- sal |>
  mutate(
    experience_level = factor(
      as.character(experience_level),
      levels = levels
    ),
    company_size = factor(
      company_size,
      levels = c("S", "M", "L"),
      labels = c("Small", "Medium", "Large")
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(experience_level),
    !is.na(company_size)
  )

# Salary medians for individual company sizes
career_size <- salary_data |>
  group_by(work_year, company_size, experience_level) |>
  summarise(
    median_salary = median(salary_in_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(salary_in_usd)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 5) |>
  mutate(company_size = as.character(company_size))

# Overall salary medians
career_all <- salary_data |>
  group_by(work_year, experience_level) |>
  summarise(
    median_salary = median(salary_in_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = sum(!is.na(salary_in_usd)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n >= 5) |>
  mutate(company_size = "All Companies")

career_plot <- bind_rows(career_all, career_size)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Salary progression table (2024-2025)
# --------------------------------------------------

career_gains <- salary_data |>
  filter(
    work_year %in% c(2024, 2025),
    !is.na(salary_in_usd)
  ) |>
  group_by(company_size, experience_level) |>
  summarise(
    median_salary = median(salary_in_usd),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    median_salary = if_else(
      n >= 5,
      median_salary,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = experience_level,
    values_from = median_salary
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Entry_Mid = (Mid - Entry) / Entry,
    Mid_Senior = (Senior - Mid) / Mid,
    Senior_Executive = (Executive - Senior) / Senior
  ) |>
  arrange(company_size)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Professional visual styling
# --------------------------------------------------

colors <- c(
  Entry = "#168B78",
  Mid = "#DF742D",
  Senior = "#416FB9",
  Executive = "#8752AA"
)

dash_styles <- c(
  Entry = "solid",
  Mid = "dash",
  Senior = "dot",
  Executive = "dashdot"
)

symbols <- c(
  Entry = "circle",
  Mid = "square",
  Senior = "diamond",
  Executive = "triangle-up"
)

navy <- "#172543"
muted <- "#596D8B"
grid_color <- "#E7EDF5"

# Format missing values as N/A
format_salary <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x),
    "N/A",
    dollar(x, accuracy = 1)
  )
}

format_gain <- function(x) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(x) | !is.finite(x),
    "N/A",
    percent(x, accuracy = 0.1)
  )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Create Plotly figure
# --------------------------------------------------

fig <- plot_ly()

trace_sizes <- character()
trace_levels <- character()

# Add one trace for each company size and level
for (size in sizes) {

  for (level in levels) {

    df <- career_plot |>
      filter(
        company_size == size,
        experience_level == level
      ) |>
      arrange(work_year)

    if (nrow(df) == 0) next

    fig <- fig |>
      add_trace(
        data = df,
        x = ~work_year,
        y = ~median_salary,
        type = "scatter",
        mode = "lines+markers",

        name = paste(level, "Level"),
        legendgroup = level,

        visible = size == "All Companies",
        showlegend = size == "All Companies",

        line = list(
          color = colors[[level]],
          width = 3,
          dash = dash_styles[[level]]
        ),

        marker = list(
          color = colors[[level]],
          symbol = symbols[[level]],
          size = 8
        ),

        text = ~paste0(
          "<b>Year:</b> ", work_year,
          "<br><b>Company size:</b> ", company_size,
          "<br><b>Experience:</b> ", experience_level,
          "<br><b>Median salary:</b> ",
          dollar(median_salary),
          "<br><b>Records:</b> ", comma(n)
        ),

        hoverinfo = "text"
      )

    trace_sizes <- c(trace_sizes, size)
    trace_levels <- c(trace_levels, level)
  }
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Add tables to the same Plotly figure
# --------------------------------------------------

# Build traces once before adding tables
fig <- plotly_build(fig)

n_lines <- length(fig$x$data)

# One table per company-size selection
for (size in sizes) {

  df <- if (size == "All Companies") {
    career_gains
  } else {
    career_gains |>
      filter(as.character(company_size) == size)
  }

  row_colors <- rep(
    c("#FFFFFF", "#F0F4F9"),
    length.out = nrow(df)
  )

  fig <- fig |>
    add_trace(
      type = "table",
      inherit = FALSE,

      domain = list(
        x = c(0, 1),
        y = c(0.04, 0.27)
      ),

      header = list(
        values = c(
          "<b>Company<br>Size</b>",
          "<b>Entry<br>Level</b>",
          "<b>Mid<br>Level</b>",
          "<b>Senior<br>Level</b>",
          "<b>Executive<br>Level</b>",
          "<b>Entry to<br>Mid (%)</b>",
          "<b>Mid to<br>Senior (%)</b>",
          "<b>Senior to<br>Executive (%)</b>"
        ),

        align = "center",
        fill = list(color = "#34445C"),
        font = list(
          color = "#FFFFFF",
          size = 12
        ),
        line = list(color = "#DCE4EF"),
        height = 48
      ),

      cells = list(
        values = list(
          as.character(df$company_size),
          format_salary(df$Entry),
          format_salary(df$Mid),
          format_salary(df$Senior),
          format_salary(df$Executive),
          format_gain(df$Entry_Mid),
          format_gain(df$Mid_Senior),
          format_gain(df$Senior_Executive)
        ),

        align = "center",
        fill = list(
            color = rep(
              list(row_colors),
              8
            )
          ),
        font = list(
          color = navy,
          size = 12
        ),
        line = list(color = "#DCE4EF"),
        height = 37
      ),

      visible = size == "All Companies",
      showlegend = FALSE
    )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Dropdown controls graph and table
# --------------------------------------------------

buttons <- lapply(seq_along(sizes), function(i) {

  selected_size <- sizes[i]

  line_visible <- trace_sizes == selected_size
  table_visible <- seq_along(sizes) == i

  # Only show one legend item per experience level
  legend_visible <- rep(FALSE, n_lines)
  shown_levels <- character()

  for (j in seq_len(n_lines)) {

    if (
      line_visible[j] &&
      !(trace_levels[j] %in% shown_levels)
    ) {

      legend_visible[j] <- TRUE

      shown_levels <- c(
        shown_levels,
        trace_levels[j]
      )
    }
  }

  list(
    label = selected_size,
    method = "update",

    args = list(
      list(
        visible = c(
          line_visible,
          table_visible
        ),

        showlegend = c(
          legend_visible,
          rep(FALSE, length(sizes))
        )
      )
    )
  )
})

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Final combined chart and table
# --------------------------------------------------

fig <- fig |>
  layout(

    paper_bgcolor = "#FFFFFF",
    plot_bgcolor = "#FFFFFF",

    font = list(
      family = "Arial, sans-serif",
      color = navy,
      size = 13
    ),

    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "<b>Median salaries generally rose across ",
        "experience levels, 2020–2025</b>"
      ),
      x = 0.5,
      xanchor = "center",
      font = list(
        size = 25,
        color = navy
      )
    ),

    xaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Year",
        standoff = 12
      ),
      dtick = 1,
      tickmode = "linear",
      domain = c(0.05, 0.82),
      showgrid = FALSE,
      zeroline = FALSE,
      linecolor = "#CBD5E1",
      tickfont = list(size = 12)
    ),

    yaxis = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Median Annual Salary (USD)",
        standoff = 12
      ),

      domain = c(0.44, 0.94),
      rangemode = "tozero",
      tickprefix = "$",
      tickformat = ",.0f",

      showgrid = TRUE,
      gridcolor = grid_color,
      zeroline = FALSE,

      tickfont = list(size = 12)
    ),

    legend = list(
      x = 0.84,
      y = 0.84,
      xanchor = "left",
      yanchor = "top",
      bgcolor = "rgba(255,255,255,0)",
      font = list(size = 12),
      tracegroupgap = 8
    ),

    updatemenus = list(
      list(
        buttons = buttons,
        direction = "down",
        x = 0.05,
        y = 0.98,
        xanchor = "left",
        yanchor = "top",
        showactive = TRUE,

        bgcolor = "#FFFFFF",
        bordercolor = "#D4DEEB",

        font = list(
          size = 12,
          color = navy
        )
      )
    ),

    annotations = list(

      list(
        text = paste0(
          "Median annual salary in USD; ",
          "at least 5 records per plotted point"
        ),
        x = 0.05,
        y = 1.03,
        xref = "paper",
        yref = "paper",
        xanchor = "left",
        showarrow = FALSE,
        font = list(
          size = 16,
          color = muted
        )
      ),

      list(
        text = paste0(
          "<b>Salary Premiums ",
          "Differ Across Company Sizes</b>"
        ),
        x = 0.5,
        y = 0.365,
        xref = "paper",
        yref = "paper",
        showarrow = FALSE,
        font = list(
          size = 22,
          color = navy
        )
      ),

      list(
        text = paste0(
          "2024–2025 salary medians and ",
          "career-stage differences"
        ),
        x = 0.5,
        y = 0.325,
        xref = "paper",
        yref = "paper",
        showarrow = FALSE,
        font = list(
          size = 15,
          color = muted
        )
      )
    ),

    height = 1100,
    autosize = TRUE,

    margin = list(
      t = 80,
      b = 40,
      l = 100,
      r = 35
    ),

    hovermode = "closest"
  ) |>
  config(
    responsive = TRUE,
    displaylogo = FALSE,
    displayModeBar = "hover"
  )

# Display exactly once
fig
```



### Key Findings

The salary data indicate that median compensation generally increases
with experience level. However, the size of the premium varies
substantially across company sizes.

Small companies show a 48.1% difference between mid-level and senior
median salaries, compared with 24.6% at medium companies and 22.5%
at large companies.

These differences suggest that company size may influence the
compensation associated with career advancement, although they do not
represent individual salary increases.

### Methodology and Limitations

Salary figures represent median annual compensation in USD.

- **Time period:** 2020–2025 for the chart; 2024–2025 for the table.
- **Grouping:** Experience level, company size, and year.
- **Minimum sample:** Five valid salary observations per chart data point.
- **Salary premiums:** Percentage differences between experience-group medians.
- **N/A:** Insufficient observations or unavailable data.

**Interpretation:** Salary premiums compare different employee groups
rather than tracking salary increases for individual employees.
Changes over time may also reflect changes in the composition of
the dataset.
